messages:
maria-ops: Heads up — p95 latency jumped ~2.6x right after canary started for model v2.3 (tokenizer update). Noticed around 10:04 UTC.
kevin-runtime: I'm pulling traces now. Seeing a lot of kernel fallback logs on hosts gpu-24-*. Traces show selected_kernel=attn_fused_fp16 then fallback to attn_generic_fp16 on the same request.
kevin-runtime: Quick snippet from host gpu-24-11 profiler: 
```
[2026-03-18T10:03:58Z] request_id=abc123 model=v2.3 seq_len=512 selected_kernel=attn_fused_fp16 exec_time=8.2ms
[2026-03-18T10:03:58Z] request_id=abc123 fallback=attn_generic_fp16 exec_time=41.7ms reason=kernel_mismatch
```
kevin-runtime: Batcher metrics also odd — micro-batches of size 1-2 despite throughput being normal. batch_timeout_ms=20.
kevin-runtime: Running kvcache hitrate check now: 
```
$ curl -s http://localhost:9200/debug/kvcache/hitrate | jq .
{"hit_rate": 0.48, "p99_miss_burst": 12}
```
maria-ops: That hit_rate is lower than usual (normally ~0.9). Could tokenizer change produce more variable prefixes? @sasha-ml any insight on tokenization?
sasha-ml: The v2.3 tokenizer splits some long tokens differently — average token count per input up ~38%. That would increase effective seq_len and change prefix overlap (kv cache less effective).
sasha-ml: Also noticed new special-char normalization path that touches preproc, causing occasional short-lived tokenization stalls.
oliver: Relatedly, host gpu-24-11 shows repeated KV cache eviction logs: 
```
[evict] tenant=t-44 freed_pages=120 reserved_kv_mb=512->256
[evict] reason=memory_pressure noisy_tenant=t-44
```
oliver: t-44 had a sudden burst of large batched rerank jobs at 10:02 that likely forced small micro-batches elsewhere.
tanvi-oncall: Deploy bot shows canary ramp events: 
```
deploy-bot: canary_start model=v2.3 pct=5 time=10:00:00Z
deploy-bot: canary_ramp model=v2.3 pct=50 time=10:02:30Z
```
maria-ops: So hypothesis: tokenizer change -> longer/varied seq lengths -> kernel selection heuristics pick fused kernel but runtime falls back due to memory layout mismatch on some seq shapes, plus noisy tenant caused KV eviction -> low cache hit rate -> more work per request -> micro-batching and fallback thrash -> p95 spike.
kevin-runtime: I reproduced locally: when seq_len distribution has a heavy tail, our kernel selector doesn't consider the combined memory pressure and alignment constraints — it attempts fused kernel then falls back at runtime. Patch candidate: check kv_reserved and alignment before selecting fused kernel.
kevin-runtime: Short mitigation: rolling back tokenizer change for canary, and pin kernel_selector to prefer generic kernel for v2.3 canary hosts until we patch. Also increase batch_timeout_ms to 50ms to allow batching to absorb the noisy bursts.
sasha-ml: Rolling back tokenizer is fine for now. We'll open a follow-up to rework tokenization normalization to avoid splitting patterns that inflate token counts.
maria-ops: Initiating rollback of v2.3 canary to v2.2 on affected clusters now. @deploy-bot can you confirm rollback steps?
deploy-bot: rollback_triggered model=v2.3 -> v2.2 scope=canary hosts=gpu-24-* time=10:08:12Z
kevin-runtime: Kicking a hotfix that forces kernel_selector_override=generic_attn_fp16 on the canary fleet and increasing batch timeout to 50ms. Patch id: PR#4928.
kevin-runtime: Uploading profiler dump to /tmp/profiles/1772460000.tar.gz for postmortem.
kevin-runtime: For the follow-up I recommend: 1) kernel selector rewrite to consider kv_reservation and seq_len_tail, 2) expose per-tenant reservation metrics to SLOs, 3) add a heuristic to avoid fused kernel selection if p99_seq_len > threshold.
oliver: Also add an alert for sudden drop in kvcache hitrate (delta > 0.2 in 5min) — would have caught this earlier.
tanvi-oncall: After rollback, p95 back to normal within ~6min. I'll keep the incident open and create postmortem link. :thumbsup:
maria-ops: Great. Filing incident and action items. Thanks all — let's sync on fixes in tomorrow's eng-runtime weekly.
